runs.t: Amdahl's Law bounds the speedup of a workload when only part can be parallelized. With serial fraction s and p processors, idealized speedup is 1 divided by (s plus (1 minus s) divided by p).

Measure how much work remains serial, then include actual parallel overhead, communication and contention. Even infinite processors cannot eliminate the serial fraction; optimize the bottleneck before adding workers.
If 20% of a report is serial, the theoretical maximum speedup is 5 times regardless of added workers. Database contention may lower it further.
Amdahl assumes a fixed workload and idealized parallel execution; real workloads can grow and require Gustafson-style scaling analysis. Do not confuse latency speedup with throughput increase.
